name: Process vs Thread Architecture
ground_truth_criteria: Process has independent address space; threads share process address space, heap, and open files
Each thread maintains its own program counter, stack, and registers
Context switching overhead is substantially higher for processes than threads

name: CPU Scheduling Fundamentals
ground_truth_criteria: Distinguishes preemptive vs non-preemptive scheduling algorithms
Explains FCFS convoy effect and Round-Robin time quantum trade-offs
Defines turnaround time, waiting time, and response time correctly

name: Race Conditions & Critical Sections
ground_truth_criteria: Defines race condition as concurrent uncoordinated access to shared memory
States the three critical section requirements: Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting
Explains atomic operations like Test-and-Set or Compare-and-Swap

name: Mutexes and Semaphores
ground_truth_criteria: Mutex has an ownership concept; counting/binary semaphores are signaling mechanisms
Explains atomic wait()/P() decrement and signal()/V() increment operations
Identifies priority inversion risks and priority inheritance solutions

name: Deadlock Characterization & Coffman Conditions
ground_truth_criteria: Explicitly names all four Coffman conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait
Explains that all four conditions must hold simultaneously for a deadlock to occur
Differentiates between resource deadlock and starvation

name: Banker's Algorithm & Deadlock Avoidance
ground_truth_criteria: Requires advance knowledge of maximum resource allocation requests per process
Maintains Available, Max, Allocation, and Need matrices (Need = Max - Allocation)
Defines a safe state where a safe execution sequence of all processes exists
